brief: A two-storey storage tower for a workbench with at least two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Base cells at level 0 (0,0), (1,0), with cell (0,0) stacked with a full base at level 1 (piece:0,0,1). Two storeys tall, with a two-compartment bin (bin:0,0,1) in the upper storey. Caps and joint bolt added by capOpenFaces/lockJoints; check_build reports no issues and meshClash clear.
Lowest storey is level 0, so the tower's base sits flat on the bench; no part is placed underneath it.
Two notch drawer frames on level 0: notch:0#0,1#notch1 (hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm) and notch:0#1,-1#notch4 (hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf), each filling an empty position between bases.

requirements.requirement: Material suitability, load rating for drawers/shelves
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks fit and collisions only; I cannot verify the printed material's strength or load capacity.

finish.summary: Built a two-storey tower on a workbench: three base cells on the lower storey, one base stacked above, two notch drawers on the lower storey, and a two-compartment bin in the upper storey. Caps and joint bolts are applied and check_build is clean with meshClash clear. The upper storey has one bin rather than drawers; drawers are on the lower storey only. Material and load performance are not verified.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
